notes: Loop 3 re-check (loop 2: 8.1). I read the README ('For judges'), the landing page (DE, EN), /r#demo, /r#demo-ai (DE, EN, phone), /r#demo-result, /r#demo-price, the /try phone run with its report and rehearsal, and connect-beta. The weakest point is mostly fixed. /r#demo-ai ships a rehearsal played by Claude subagents (src/report/demo-ai.json, tracked), dated and labelled. Its first card says 'Von einer KI: die ausgedachten Gäste gespielt … Gerechnet hat einfacher Code' (report-ai.txt:59). The six AI answers are distinct and in character (Paweł's 7,90 €, Greta's Mensa). The landing page turns this into a transferable AI lesson: 'Wer die Gäste spielt, verändert die Geschichte'. /try now reaches a rule-based rehearsal without an AI app (try-rehearsal.txt:22-30). The price demo really works out the 2027 wage rise: 60 h × 0,70 € = 42 € a week (report-price.txt:216). 117/117 checks pass. Held back: the comparison uses a different cast (rules: Thanh, Fatima…; Claude: Noor, Chiara, Paweł…), so 'the same rehearsal' is not true. The AI's words are behind taps and stay German for an English judge. There is no live URL yet, README.md:57 and :204 still promise a 401 the server no longer sends, and no real owner has used it. No cap applies.
improvements: /r#demo-ai, step 5 (src/report/rehearsal.ts, site/src/report.ts; report-ai.txt:413-414; report-ai-phone.png slices 5-6): put the AI's own work on screen without a tap. On this demo, open two interview answers by default with a 'von Claude geschrieben' tag, for example Paweł ('Bei etwa 8 € … würde ich es probieren') and Greta ('Unter 7,20 € würde ich es probieren'). Beside one of them, show the brief Claude got: 'Das wusste Claude: Paweł, zahlt sonst 7,90 € für Suppe und Flat White … Das wusste Claude nicht: Ihre Kosten, Ihre Gewinnschwelle.' Add a 'Zum Probelauf springen' link to the ribbon, because step 5 is about 6,000 px down on a phone. For EN, ES and PL readers, put a saved translation under the German original and label it as one (report-ai-en.txt:12: an English judge sees only German). Why: use of AI and its limits are scored. Today the AI's output is the one thing a judge has to hunt for, and the brief would teach what a model sees and what it does not. Done when report-ai-phone.png shows two AI-written sentences and the brief without a tap, and report-ai-en.txt has an English line beside each.

Landing page and AI ribbon (site/src/messages.ts:369 'See the same rehearsal played by Claude (AI)', DE 'Denselben Probelauf ansehen'; :370 and the ribbon text in report-ai.txt:12): make the comparison between rules and Claude controlled and honest. The rule-based demo plays Thanh, Fatima, Sofia, Leyla, Murat and Noor (seed 8, report.txt:371-433). The Claude run plays Noor, Chiara, Paweł, Murat, Greta and Jan (src/report/demo-ai.json). So it is not 'the same rehearsal', and two different casts cannot show that 'Wer die Gäste spielt, verändert die Geschichte'. Run the fixed rules on the AI file's own cast and event (the same six people, the same rival café before round 3). Then show one row on /r#demo-ai: 'Dieselben 6 Gäste: feste Regeln x probiert, y erzählt · Claude 3 probiert, 0 erzählt'. Until then, say 'derselbe Mittagstisch, andere Gäste'. Why: this is the project's best transferable AI lesson, and a judge who compares the names will doubt it. Done when the comparison keeps the cast the same and a test pins it.

README first screen and the default demo (README.md:7, :57, :204; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:159; src/report/messages.ts:129 who.ai.demo; report.txt:64). After the deploy, put the live /, /r#demo-ai and /try links in the first lines. Remove the 401 claims: README.md:57 says 'the server answers HTTP 401', but src/mcp/http.ts:13 says it never does (mcp-beta-oauth), so a judge who connects the MCP with the README in hand expects the wrong thing. On /r#demo, change 'Von einer KI: in dieser Demo gar nichts' to '… gar nichts. Dieselben Schritte mit von Claude gespielten Gästen ansehen →'. Why: execution and demo. The first demo a judge clicks still says the AI did nothing and does not point to where it did something. Done when the README has live links and no '401', and the who-did-what line on /r#demo links to /r#demo-ai.

Facts card and 'Was Sie über KI gelernt haben' (report.txt:150-166 and the take-home line; src/report/sections.ts): finish the lesson that public facts carry a date. The card now says 'Öffentliche Regeln, auf die sich die Rechnung stützt. Prüfen Sie im Zweifel die Quelle' and gives 'Stand:' dates. But the facts wear no chip, and the take-home still names four kinds ('Von Ihnen, berechnet, geschätzt oder ausgedacht?'). Add a fifth chip, 'Öffentliche Regel · Stand 1. Januar 2026', and one line in the AI lesson: 'Was eine KI über Steuern oder Löhne weiß, hat ein Datum. Prüfen Sie es an der Quelle.' Why: the January 2026 VAT change is a concrete, local example of a model's knowledge going stale, which is transferable AI literacy. Done when the take-home names five kinds and the facts card wears its chip in all four languages.

Proof of use (README; docs/09-pitch-videos.md:38 'no real café has used it yet'). Before the submission, run one invite-code session with a real Berlin café owner on /try. Add a dated note, with her consent: her break-even in her own words, the guess she changed, and whether she would run the test. Never invent a quote. Why: impact on the named audience is still argued, not shown. vision.md calls this the strongest proof, and PRD.md:200-202 already defines the note. Done when the README links to one dated session note from a real owner.
pitchIn60s: What-IF teaches Berlin café owners to rehearse a decision before they spend money, in German, English, Spanish and Polish. It works through an MCP connector, a skill, or a /try page that needs no AI app. A 'what if' becomes a six-step visual lesson. Every number is labelled as yours, calculated, a guess or imagined, and code does every sum, net of the 2026 VAT. You guess the break-even before it is shown, then a slider explains why it moves. Imagined customers from your Kiez produce questions, never forecasts. A fourth demo shows the lunch deal's customers played by Claude subagents, labelled and dated, and the site draws the sharpest AI lesson in the room from it: who plays the customers changes the story, so they are not data. It ends in a printable 10-day test with a keep, tweak or stop rule agreed in advance, and an after-the-test page puts reality on the same line as your guesses. The gaps: no live link or real owner yet, and the comparison between rules and AI uses two different casts.
standout: The honest contrast between rules and Claude. The AI-played run (3 of 6 tried, 0 of 6 told, report-ai-en.txt:272-279) differs from the rule-based demo, and the site uses that difference to teach that imagined customers are not data. Add the guess-first break-even and the keep, tweak or stop rule agreed before the test, closed by /r#demo-result, and it teaches both the decision and the limits of AI.
weakest: Proof and comparability. No real owner has used it, the README has no live URL yet, and the AI lesson compares two different casts while calling it 'the same rehearsal'.
